body:
DEFENSE: separate origins do NOT block placement; they block DOM control, which we should deliberately replace with server lifecycle.

Exact launch flow: (1) Setup step A asks `console.example` for `getScreenDetails()` / `window-management` permission. (2) After permission resolves, require a second explicit `Open audience display` click so popup transient activation is fresh. In that click call `window.open('https://audience.example/display/<non-secret launch_id>', '_blank', 'popup,noopener,noreferrer,left=<screen.availLeft>,top=<screen.availTop>,width=<screen.availWidth>,height=<screen.availHeight>')`. Cross-origin navigation does not prevent `window.open` from selecting coordinates. Browsers may clamp/block it, and Window Management is limited/experimental, so manual drag-to-projector is mandatory fallback. (3) Audience connects to SAME-ORIGIN `wss://audience.example/ws` (reverse-proxied backend), consumes only public DTOs, and reports `ready/heartbeat/disconnected` through backend. Console uses `wss://console.example/ws`; server mediates commands/state with role auth. No BroadcastChannel/postMessage/client peer channel. (4) Fullscreen cannot be invoked by console on a cross-origin child. The target audience document needs its own click (`Enter fullscreen`) and calls `document.documentElement.requestFullscreen()`; because popup is already on target screen, default current screen suffices. `requestFullscreen({screen})` is experimental and still needs user activation, so do not make it a dependency. (5) Console observes display connection/size/fullscreen via WSS. Authorized `display.close` makes script-opened audience call `window.close()` itself; focus/close are best effort and never security controls.

Opener/COOP tradeoff: recommended `COOP: same-origin` on BOTH origins plus `noopener,noreferrer`; accept that console gets no usable WindowProxy (`closed/focus/close` unavailable) and use WSS health instead. This removes reverse-tabnabbing/opener navigation and prevents an audience XSS from reaching the console WindowProxy. The weaker alternative—console `COOP: same-origin-allow-popups`, audience `unsafe-none`, retain WindowProxy for `.closed/.close/.focus`—preserves convenience but creates a cross-origin opener bridge and is not worth it. Do not send a bearer token in launch URL: launch_id only correlates a provisional public display; if audience content is access-controlled, complete a separate one-use display pairing and issue an HttpOnly display cookie before content.

Topology safety: subscribe to `screenschange`/`currentscreenchange`; any removal, current-screen change, or mirror/extend uncertainty triggers `DISPLAY NEEDS CONFIRMATION`, never moves private state into audience. Audience remains public-only; console hides private panes behind a privacy curtain until re-confirmed.

Sources: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window_Management_API ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/open ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/requestFullscreen ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/WebSocket_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Broadcast_Channel_API
